identity: Neutral N-C-O radical, CAS 22400-26-6, linear X2Pi ground electronic manifold. It is not cyanate anion NCO-, CON/CNO connectivity variants, or the closed-shell HNCO molecule. JANAF C-087, NASA NCO and the ATcT gas record refer to the same neutral radical, resolving the appendix identity exclusion.
recommendation: Prioritize a retained-thermal ATcT energy candidate for NCO. Its large outdated atomization-energy offset is clear after exact identity matching, while a thermal replacement requires a separate rovibronic assessment.
science: The original JANAF page 635 was visually inspected: the 1970 evaluation adopts Hf(0) about 159.0 kJ/mol from early photodissociation and competing estimates. The current ATcT value is 127.03 kJ/mol. Balanced against same-version atoms, the atomization-energy increase is 31.984 kJ/mol: retained-thermal K rises by 12.9945 at 1500 K and 2.61613 at 4000 K. The inherited fit reproduces JANAF to within 1.25%; aligned JANAF/NASA thermal ratios are only 1.02286-1.03818, so this is primarily an energy problem.
modern: NASA cites East 1993 and moves the energy substantially toward later experiment/theory, but remains 4.411 kJ/mol below the current balanced ATcT atomization energy. The 2004 focal-point study and the 1996 HNCO threshold paper are present in the current ATcT provenance; their abstracts were inspected, not all original derivations. Current ATcT includes direct NCO dissociation and HNCO-to-NCO thresholds, so the update is not justified merely by the date of the database.
importance: NCO is an intermediate connecting carbon and reactive nitrogen in combustion and atmospheric chemistry. The current finite hot reducing equilibrium grid contains very little NCO; this does not estimate non-equilibrium reaction fluxes.
conventions: The JANAF page explicitly includes X2Pi spin-orbit components at 0 and 95.6 cm-1 with weights two each, plus higher electronic entries. Do not multiply its thermochemistry by another doublet or Pi degeneracy. A future thermal model must retain spin-orbit and vibronic contributions consistently; principal-isotope spin weights and translational masses require explicit normalization.
followup: Construct the physical ATcT-minus-JANAF energy shift, preserving inherited thermal shape and fit residual, then run fixed-network substitutions. Include a joint HNCO/NCO diagnostic after separate tests. If replacing thermal functions later, investigate the few-percent aligned thermal difference independently of the much larger energy correction.
